Patches the runtime trust store against the eMudhra intermediate-CA
compromise. No application code changes and no migration — pull the new image
and recreate the container.

## What happened

Eight eMudhra intermediate certificates were compromised through weak key
generation, and every major root program distrusted them in October 2026. Any
TLS client still trusting those intermediates can be impersonated by anyone
holding the recovered keys. This app makes outbound TLS on every Plex,
ThemerrDB, and poster request, so its trust store is on the critical path.

## What changed

- `castore` bumped to `1.0.22`, which removes the compromised intermediates
  from the bundled CA file the Elixir release ships.
- Runner base moved to `debian:bookworm-20261020-slim`, past the fixed
  `ca-certificates`, so the OS store (`/etc/ssl/certs`) the runtime falls back
  to is clean as well. The builder image stays on its snapshot (hexpm has not
  published a newer one for this Elixir/OTP combo) — both are bookworm, so the
  pair stays glibc-compatible, and both stages install `ca-certificates`
  fresh at build time regardless.

## Upgrading

Pull the new image and recreate the container. No database migration, no config
change.
